diff_ref: commit 3a9b4495 -- scripts/code_map/thresholds.py (new) and the gb additions to tests/test_code_map.py (8 new TestCase classes / 12 test methods + helpers)

smells.finding: Each new test method is a single, focused assertion sequence (roughly 10-30 lines); the longest, ChurnRatioFalsifierTests.test_churn_ceiling_trips_when_a_corpus_wide_count_leaks_into_every_page, stays readable because every line is one measurement step.
The 8 new TestCase classes are each narrowly scoped to one threshold family's positive or falsifier case (30-75 lines); none accumulates unrelated responsibilities.

HoleRatioBaselineTests.setUpClass, RecallFloorTests.setUpClass and ChurnRatioTests._build all repeat the same tempfile+subprocess/cli.main build-and-load idiom already used by dozens of pre-existing TestCase classes in this same file (RenderReportTests, DeterminismTests, InboundAttributionTests, etc.).

override.repo_standard: global-crew.md 'Implementation discipline': match the surrounding code's naming, labeling, and in-file documentation conventions -- the project's specific conventions are the local delta.
override.reason: This file's own established idiom, used consistently across ~15 pre-existing test classes, IS the documented local convention; introducing a shared helper here would diverge from the file's own pattern rather than follow it, and the file's own docstring comment for _bucket_line already states the file's actual rule about factoring only when there is exactly one true source of an invariant -- setup boilerplate is not that.

smells.finding: RECALL_GROUND_TRUTH's (caller, callee) tuples are a legitimate hand-labeled data table, not an ad hoc clump of parameters passed around together.
The four thresholds are genuinely scalar ratios/floors; a float or a small str-keyed dict is the right shape for them, not an underuse of a richer type.
Every new helper (_make_recall_fixture_repo(tmp), _diff_line_count(a_text, b_text), _map_diff_lines(root_a, root_b), _template_literal_constants(source)) takes 1-2 parameters.
thresholds.py has exactly one reason to change: a committed number or invariant moving. The test additions each have exactly one reason to change: their own family's threshold or fixture.

thresholds.RECALL_FLOOR_DERIVATION (thresholds.py lines 82-87) is a string constant restating, almost verbatim, what RECALL_FLOORS's own docstring comment already says two lines above it -- and it is never read by any test, check, or doc (grep across scripts/ and tests/ finds only its own definition). It is dead data authored for a consumer that does not exist. Not a blocker: it is inert, not misleading, and cheap to delete or wire in later -- flagged as a triage-worthy cleanup, not a threshold-usefulness defect.

thresholds.py's docstrings are dense but carry information code cannot express (measured values, provenance, the gate's own history, the mandated WHEN THIS FIRES action) -- this is the ruling-mandated shape for this file, not a substitute for clearer code.
